chapter: Leaving the band, Strayhorn and reflections
title: Why he left the band in 1950 and Norman Granz's version
summary: Greer says he left because of his wife, not Granz, and describes the small group while Duke was in Europe.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Now, I'm going to turn the tape recorder off because I don't want to read you this version of how you left the band. I want to see what you think, find out whether
it's correct.
(Recording interruption.)
Okay, I just read Mr. Greer the version of his leaving the band, that Derek Jewell (illegible) relates in his book, "Portrait of Duke Ellington".
The reason I left the band, when I come back to New York from Europe --

Right. My wife was (unintelligible), you know. So it was a toss up between I stay with my wife and the band. Naturally, I stayed with my wife. We were good friends until he died. You know, Duke -- I didn't have to ask Duke for no money. Duke was never -- there's one word I say for Duke, the word "no", he didn't use that. The guys will verify if you ever was to ask someone, no matter what money they want, he would never say no. No matter the amount of money, he didn't know how to say no, because they were his family, the band. That was his first love. And the guy, he never was a man that valued money above everything else. You understand? And the guys could go to Duke and any amount of money that was necessary, they could get it.

Well, now Norman Granz says, they also quote Norman Granz as saving, "Sure, I pulled Johnny and the others out of the band. I'd been very close to him ever since 1941 when "Jump For Joy" was in Los Angeles. I was doing my

first jam sessions out there. I used him on jam sessions and from time to time after the war I was in at Duke's band concerts. I felt Johnny was kept down in the band. I wanted to record him outside the Ellington context, and that's why he and the others came out. Harry Carney almost came too, but he was afraid to quit, and anyway, we didn't need him. Johnny's band had one big hit, it was 'Castle Rock', which was like a Louis Jordan thing with no singing. After a time Greer didn't want to travel so we used Sam Woodyard (PHONETIC) on drums and Aaron Bell (PHONETIC) on bass. It was a good band."
So now according to him, he pulled you all out of the band.

No, no way. How the hell could he pull us out of the band? No, he didn't pull us out of no band. Never. The way -- the first time -- they wanted Duke just to go to Europe on something they had over there. So he went and the only one he take with him was Ray Nance, that's all. And one of the singers, Joy Sherrill. So Billy stayed home, Johnny, and Lawrence Brown and I forget who, it was somebody on bass who -- who the hell played bass with us?
Aaron Belle?
No, no. I think it was Jimmy Blanton's cousin, what's his name. Bass player.
Okay, we can get that.
Well, anyway, we had a five or six piece

band, it would play (unintelligible). People went crazy. We played the Apollo up here, you know, cabaret, club...., had Tyree on the xylophone, we had a tough band. We were something else. So when Duke come back and he heard it he said, oh, no, you know. So some of the guys went back with him, you know. But I had made up my mind I wasn't traveling because it was more important that I be here with my wife.
We never -- we parted friends.
So Norman Granz wasn't connected with it?

No way. Norman Granz, he may have tried to pull somebody, but he didn't have that influence to do that. Because the guys may have played, recorded with him or something like that. But travel with him? No way. No way.
Now, those guys were out of the band for about three years, though.
Who?

Johnny Hodges. Johnny Hodges was out of the band from about 1951 to about 1954. And he replaced him with Willie Smith. And Lawrence Brown was out a little bit longer than that, I think. He came in much later.

I was out, '52. I don't recall. I don't recall when he left or why they left or what it was all about. Because, I don't know, I don't remember. I really don't remember. I couldn't be quoted as saying nothing like that. No way.
